terms.name: instance
terms.means: A hub with its store on a server, shared by an institution or a project; the general word for it.

terms.name: the instance's own name
terms.means: What a sentence says when it names the shared installation: the name the instance gives itself, written <instance> in a label.

terms.name: desktop hub
terms.means: The hub Armature Desktop runs on a person's computer, which holds the workspaces.

terms.name: the hub
terms.means: The desktop hub, as Armature Desktop's own window calls it.

terms.name: hub
terms.means: One host bound to one store: the address a client talks to.

terms.name: Armature Desktop
terms.means: The product's name for the installed app.

terms.name: the desktop app
terms.means: Armature Desktop in running text; "the app" once it has been named.

terms.name: the viewer
terms.means: Armature's own read-only web pages at an instance, as the documents call them.

terms.name: tool
terms.means: A program that reads and writes through a hub, such as Quiver, CoQui or a linter.

terms.name: client
terms.means: A tool, in developer documents.

terms.name: this computer
terms.means: The person's own computer, as opposed to the instance.

terms.name: sign-in provider
terms.means: The institution's identity service, where a person signs in.

terms.name: identity provider
terms.means: The sign-in provider, for whoever configures it.

terms.name: issuer
terms.means: The sign-in provider's OpenID Connect address, in settings and codes.

terms.name: release channel
terms.means: Where Armature Desktop looks for a new version.

terms.name: main
terms.means: The instance's shared, agreed design: the branch the shared work is merged into.

terms.name: branch
terms.means: A line of the design's history on the instance, written directly by anyone with the right and merged into.

terms.name: workspace
terms.means: A branch owned by one person and held on one computer, where their tools work, online or offline.

terms.name: linked
terms.means: A workspace belongs to one computer, and only the app on that computer may write it.

terms.name: unlinked
terms.means: A workspace belongs to no computer and can be linked to one.

terms.name: parent
terms.means: The branch a workspace started from, takes updates from and merges into; a label names that branch instead of saying "parent".

terms.name: workspace name
terms.means: The short name a person gives a workspace, such as unit-3.

terms.name: branch name
terms.means: The name the instance gives a workspace's branch, such as jdoe_unit-3.

terms.name: starting point
terms.means: The instance's commit a workspace was created at or last updated to; the first column of a conflict review.

terms.name: your workspace
terms.means: The workspace as this computer holds it; the copy has no second name.

terms.name: Older commits kept offline
terms.means: The setting for how many of the instance's older commits a workspace keeps so that reads work offline.

terms.name: workspaces folder
terms.means: Where Armature Desktop keeps workspaces on disk.

terms.name: the app's data folder
terms.means: Where Armature Desktop keeps its settings and, by default, its workspaces.

terms.name: the discarded folder
terms.means: Where a discarded workspace's files are copied before its branch is deleted.

terms.name: item bank
terms.means: A tool's view of the items in a workspace; never a word for the workspace itself.

terms.name: commit
terms.means: One recorded change to the design, with who made it, when and why; also the act of recording it.

terms.name: to push
terms.means: Commits made on this computer that are not yet on the instance: "3 to push", "Commits to push".

terms.name: latest commit
terms.means: The newest commit of a branch.

terms.name: message
terms.means: The text saying what a commit holds, on every form that takes one.

terms.name: history
terms.means: The list of commits that made a branch or changed one record.

terms.name: as of
terms.means: The design as it stood at a commit, followed by the commit's date and short identifier.

terms.name: by
terms.means: Who made a commit: "by Dana".

terms.name: for
terms.means: The person an agent acted for: "by Quiver drafter, for Dana".

terms.name: via
terms.means: The service that relayed a person's commit: "by Dana, via CoQui".

terms.name: made
terms.means: When the work was done, kept through a push.

terms.name: pushed
terms.means: When a commit reached the instance.

terms.name: Revert
terms.means: Undo a commit by making a new commit; held for that action if it is built.

terms.name: New workspace
terms.means: The heading over the form that creates a workspace.

terms.name: Create workspace
terms.means: Create a branch on the instance and hold it on this computer as a workspace.

terms.name: from main
terms.means: A new workspace starts from main, which becomes its parent.

terms.name: from another branch
terms.means: A new workspace starts from a branch other than main, which becomes its parent; never from a workspace.

terms.name: Push
terms.means: Send the commits made on this computer to the workspace's branch on the instance, each as it was made.

terms.name: Update from <parent>
terms.means: Have the instance merge the parent's new work into the workspace, then copy the result here.

terms.name: Update from <parent> first
terms.means: The words for the refusal of a merge whose parent has work the workspace has not taken in.

terms.name: Open merge request into <branch>
terms.means: Ask for a workspace or a branch to be merged into a branch.

terms.name: Merge
terms.means: Combine one branch into another; on a merge request, what whoever may merge into the target does.

terms.name: the merge request's health
terms.means: Whether a merge request would merge cleanly now, worked out on every look.

row.concept: Ask what a delivery would find

terms.name: Remove from this computer
terms.means: Take a workspace off this computer; its branch on the instance is deleted when its parent has all of it, and kept otherwise.

terms.name: Discard <n> commits and remove
terms.means: Remove a workspace and give up its commits that were never pushed; the number is in the label.

terms.name: Unlink from this computer
terms.means: Release a workspace from this computer once everything is pushed; it stays on the instance.

terms.name: Link to this computer
terms.means: Take an unlinked workspace you own onto this computer.

terms.name: Your unlinked workspaces
terms.means: The list a workspace is linked from.

terms.name: Unlink from the other computer
terms.means: Release a workspace linked to a computer that is lost or out of reach; its unpushed commits can no longer be pushed.

terms.name: conflict
terms.means: A field or part changed on both sides of a merge, or a record created on both sides with different contents.

terms.name: Keep yours
terms.means: In a conflict, keep the workspace's value.

terms.name: Take <parent>'s
terms.means: In a conflict, take the parent's value.

terms.name: Edit
terms.means: In a conflict, write a value that is neither side's.

terms.name: Start over from <parent>
terms.means: Give up a workspace's own work and begin again from its parent; held for that action if it is built.

terms.name: Look up
terms.means: Fetch and show what an address says about itself, before connecting.

terms.name: Connect
terms.means: Bind Armature Desktop to one instance.

terms.name: Sign in
terms.means: Authenticate at the sign-in provider.

terms.name: Sign out
terms.means: End the sign-in.

terms.name: Try again
terms.means: Repeat a step that did not go through.

terms.name: Pairing
terms.means: Giving a tool the pairing key so the desktop hub accepts its writes; the page that does it.

terms.name: paired tool
terms.means: A tool that holds the pairing key.

terms.name: New pairing key
terms.means: Replace the pairing key; every paired tool needs the new one.

terms.name: Pause the hub
terms.means: Stop the desktop hub answering tools until it is resumed.

row.concept: Pause, resume, start, restart the hub

terms.name: Resume the hub
terms.means: Let a paused desktop hub answer tools again.

row.concept: Pause, resume, start, restart the hub

terms.name: Start the hub
terms.means: Start the desktop hub.

row.concept: Pause, resume, start, restart the hub

terms.name: Restart the hub
terms.means: Stop the desktop hub and start it again.

row.concept: Pause, resume, start, restart the hub

terms.name: new version
terms.means: A release of Armature Desktop newer than the one installed; "update" is left to "Update from <parent>".

terms.name: Install and restart
terms.means: Install a new version of Armature Desktop.

terms.name: Look for a new version
terms.means: Ask the release channel whether a new version exists.

terms.name: Diagnostics
terms.means: The page showing Armature Desktop's diagnostic lines.

terms.name: register
terms.means: Add a person to an instance's registry.

terms.name: Ask an administrator of <instance> to register you
terms.means: The words for the refusal of a person the instance does not know.

terms.name: give a role
terms.means: Give a person a role on a branch.

terms.name: remove a role
terms.means: Withdraw a role a person holds on a branch.

terms.name: grant
terms.means: A role held on a branch, and the act of giving it, for administrators and the API.

terms.name: revoke
terms.means: Withdraw a grant, for administrators and the API.

terms.name: export
terms.means: The graph at a commit as one file, for research or reuse.

terms.name: New branch
terms.means: Create a branch on the instance for others to work toward; whoever creates it owns it.

terms.name: Update from <branch>
terms.means: Merge another branch's new work into a branch, in the same words as a workspace's update.

terms.name: merge request
terms.means: A record that someone asked for a branch or a workspace to be merged into a branch.

terms.name: Close
terms.means: End a merge request without merging it.

terms.name: All pushed
terms.means: No commits on this computer are waiting to be pushed.

terms.name: Changed elsewhere
terms.means: The workspace's own branch on the instance has commits this computer did not push.

terms.name: <parent> has updates
terms.means: The parent has work the workspace has not taken in.

terms.name: Up to date with <parent>
terms.means: The workspace holds everything its parent has.

terms.name: This workspace was changed elsewhere, and this computer's unpushed commits can no longer be pushed. You can discard them and link the workspace again.
terms.means: The message for unpushed commits that can never be pushed.

terms.name: Linked to another computer
terms.means: A write was refused because the workspace is linked to another computer.

terms.name: Not linked to this computer
terms.means: A write was refused because the workspace is linked to no computer.

terms.name: <instance> cannot be reached
terms.means: The instance did not answer.

terms.name: Offline
terms.means: The badge for an instance that does not answer.

terms.name: Not connected
terms.means: Armature Desktop has not yet been connected to an instance.

terms.name: refused
terms.means: A hub would not carry out a request; the words come first and the code second, "by <instance>" or "by this computer".

terms.name: Compatible
terms.means: This version of the app and that instance can work together.

terms.name: Not compatible
terms.means: This version of the app and that instance cannot work together.

terms.name: Not committed yet
terms.means: An edit a tool holds that is not yet valid enough to commit, shown with the rule that holds it.

terms.name: you
terms.means: The person, on a page.

terms.name: person
terms.means: Someone registered on an instance, in documents.

terms.name: your ID on <instance>
terms.means: What an instance knows a person by; one value wherever it is shown.

terms.name: handle
terms.means: The short prefix of a person's branch names; pages show the whole branch name.

terms.name: agent
terms.means: A registered non-person that writes for a person, shown by its own name.

terms.name: proposal
terms.means: What an agent writes, until the person accepts it.

terms.name: service
terms.means: A program holding its own credential on an instance.

terms.name: relay
terms.means: A service writing for a named person under a grant.

terms.name: owner
terms.means: Whoever created a branch; may write it, merge into it, delete it and make others its maintainers.

terms.name: maintainer
terms.means: May write and merge into a branch, as its owner may; for main, the only one who may merge.

terms.name: administrator
terms.means: Whoever holds the role that registers people and gives roles.

terms.name: operator
terms.means: The person who stands up and keeps an instance, and runs its repair and check tools on the server.

terms.name: reader
terms.means: Someone who reads through the viewer; not a role.

terms.name: reviewer
terms.means: Someone who signs off; not a role.

terms.name: role
terms.means: What a person may do on a branch: owner, maintainer or administrator.

terms.name: your sign-in
terms.means: What Armature Desktop keeps in the keychain to act as the person.

terms.name: instance details
terms.means: An instance's name, its address and who signs people in, confirmed before connecting.

row.concept: What the instance shows before connecting

terms.name: The instance's details changed since you looked them up
terms.means: The words for the refusal of a connection whose instance details are no longer the ones confirmed.

row.concept: What the instance shows before connecting

terms.name: the instance's name
terms.means: The name an instance gives itself, used as its name everywhere.

terms.name: address
terms.means: Where the instance's API answers.

terms.name: pairing key
terms.means: The secret a tool sends with every write to the desktop hub.

terms.name: No sign-in (for testing only)
terms.means: An instance that trusts whoever a request says it is, for development and rehearsal.

terms.name: port
terms.means: Where the desktop hub listens.

terms.name: check
terms.means: A tool that examines work and reports on it; the word is used for nothing else.

terms.name: report
terms.means: What one check said about one commit.

terms.name: result
terms.means: What a check concluded.

terms.name: required checks
terms.means: Checks an instance requires before a merge into a branch.

terms.name: personal checks
terms.means: Checks a person requires of their own pushes.

terms.name: On
terms.means: A personal check is applied to pushes.

terms.name: override
terms.means: Go on despite a check that is waiting or failed, with a reason on record.

terms.name: Merge anyway
terms.means: Merge despite a required check, with a reason.

terms.name: Push anyway
terms.means: Push despite a personal check, with a reason.

terms.name: Reason for overriding
terms.means: The field that takes the reason for an override.

terms.name: overridden
terms.means: A check's result was overridden: "<result>, overridden".

terms.name: Waiting for a report
terms.means: A required check has not reported yet.

terms.name: event feed
terms.means: The stream of events checks listen to.

terms.name: record
terms.means: Anything in the design graph: an artifact or a relationship.

terms.name: document
terms.means: A record, in the API and its reference only.

terms.name: artifact
terms.means: A thing designed: an objective, an item, an activity, a module.

terms.name: relationship
terms.means: A link between two artifacts, kept as a record with its own rationale.

terms.name: objective
terms.means: A learning objective.

terms.name: objective state
terms.means: Where an objective stands: one of the four values reserved for it.

terms.name: item
terms.means: A reusable assessment question.

terms.name: item status
terms.means: Where an item stands: one of the four values reserved for it.

terms.name: item type
terms.means: An item's kind, shown in a spaced form.

terms.name: part
terms.means: A piece of an item.

terms.name: stem
terms.means: The part that holds an item's question text.

terms.name: option
terms.means: The part that holds one answer a learner may choose.

terms.name: placement
terms.means: An item placed in an assessment.

terms.name: placement status
terms.means: A placement's own clearance, apart from its item's status.

terms.name: assessment
terms.means: A set of placed items.

terms.name: activity
terms.means: A learning activity.

terms.name: lesson
terms.means: An ordered set of activities.

terms.name: module
terms.means: A unit of a course, holding activities, lessons and assessments.

terms.name: course
terms.means: The whole a set of modules belongs to.

terms.name: declared objective
terms.means: A module's statement that it covers an objective, with a role.

terms.name: formative use
terms.means: An item used inside an activity, not for credit.

terms.name: prerequisite
terms.means: One objective required before another, with a rationale.

terms.name: need
terms.means: A learning need.

terms.name: evidence
terms.means: What supports a learning need.

terms.name: dataset
terms.means: A set of learner data.

terms.name: measurement
terms.means: One figure taken from a dataset about a record.

terms.name: item statistic
terms.means: A measurement about an item.

terms.name: design note
terms.means: A recorded design decision with its category; always with "design".

terms.name: finding
terms.means: A concern about a record, with a status and a resolution.

terms.name: sign-off
terms.means: One person's judgment on a record as of a commit.

terms.name: out of date
terms.means: A sign-off whose record changed after it was given.

terms.name: external reference
terms.means: A record's identifier in another system.

terms.name: attachment
terms.means: A hashed pointer to bytes stored elsewhere.

terms.name: coverage
terms.means: How well a module's placements assess its declared objectives.

terms.name: level
terms.means: How well one objective is covered; a module's coverage is a level.

terms.name: alignment
terms.means: Which items assess which objectives.

terms.name: privacy level
terms.means: How much about people an export carries.

terms.name: slice
terms.means: A named subset of the graph for an export.

terms.name: rule
terms.means: A condition every write must meet, beyond what the store enforces.

terms.name: Broken rules
terms.means: What a refused write or merge lists: each rule it fails, described in words.

terms.name: version
terms.means: The installed release of Armature Desktop.

terms.name: API revision
terms.means: The date-named version of the API a hub serves and a client speaks; shown to people only in the details.

terms.name: <instance> is too old for this version of the app
terms.means: The words for the refusal of a client whose API revision is newer than the hub serves.

terms.name: Design Graph
terms.means: The drawing of the whole design.

terms.name: Coverage View
terms.means: One module's coverage.

terms.name: Focus page
terms.means: One record's neighborhood on its own page.

terms.name: Walkthrough
terms.means: A step-by-step walk from a record back to its evidence.

terms.name: lens
terms.means: A way of coloring the Design Graph.

terms.name: Changes lens
terms.means: The lens showing what a branch gained since a commit.

terms.name: figure
terms.means: An exportable drawing with a stamp.

terms.name: Work from your own computer
terms.means: The viewer's page that links to Armature Desktop.

terms.name: Module content
terms.means: A module's activities, lessons and assessments, as the viewer lists them.

terms.name: This record as the API returns it
terms.means: The title over a record shown as the hub returns it.

avoided.allowed: The Draft status of an item or an objective.
